title: no_counterexample with zero invariants is a false green — model-check must execute invariants or downgrade the verdict
description:
Reproduced: model-check reports outcome=no_counterexample with invariants_checked:[] (see specodelic/merge.check.json). A clean verdict over an empty invariant set implies verification that did not happen.

RED: test asserts that a report with invariants_checked:[] carries outcome != no_counterexample (e.g. vacuous_clean / not_checked) or fails the stage.
GREEN: per specs/model_check.md's backend contract — either execute constraint predicates (invariant-kind exprs) as stateright invariants, or label the outcome explicitly as exploratory-only (e.g. 'no_deadlock_reached') so consumers cannot read it as counterexample-free verification. Fix the TLA+ module header and stuttering so opt-in TLC runs clean.
Also: model_check.md's rerun_on_model_change transition requires the staleness fix in specodelic-8nt to be meaningful for edge edits.
Evidence: review round 2, issue 4 + path-to-prod step 2.

title: Input hardening: lint hangs forever on a FIFO named *.md and reads /dev/zero unbounded (OOM)
description:
Reproduced: mkfifo /tmp/x.md && spk lint /tmp/x.md blocks forever (timed out, exit 124); /dev/zero hits the same unbounded read path and OOM-kills (confirmed mechanism, tested under ulimit). Ingestion uses std::fs::read_to_string with no file-type or size check (src/main.rs:486 and :1110).

RED: tests — (a) lint on a FIFO named *.md returns a labeled error within a timeout, never blocks; (b) lint on an oversized regular file (> cap) returns a labeled error naming the cap.
GREEN: require f.metadata()?.is_file() (or file_type().is_file()) before reading; enforce a size cap (e.g. 2 MiB — corpus files are ~10-50 KB) with a remediation hint naming the offending path. Same treatment for compile/verify/graph ingestion paths that share the discovery code.
Evidence: review round 2, issue 6.

title: model-check: artifact consistency compares only StateValues — deleted transition edges pass silently and stale SHA is attached as provenance
description:
Reproduced 2026-09-28: assert_artifact_consistent (src/model_check.rs:329) extracts only the .tla StateValues line and compares against ir.states. Deleting a transition disjunct from specodelic/merge.tla left model-check returning identical no_counterexample / states_explored:7, and the report attached the MODIFIED file's new SHA-256 (da056432…) as artifact_sha256 provenance — the checker explored ir's transitions while claiming to have checked the on-disk module.

RED: test compiles a corpus spec, deletes one Next disjunct from the emitted .tla, runs model-check, expects stale_artifact failure (today it succeeds).
GREEN: extend assert_artifact_consistent to structurally compare the Next disjunct set (and Output function) against ir.transitions/ir.emits, or hash the full IR-vs-artifact mapping — states alone are insufficient.
REFACTOR: separate the artifact-structure extraction from the comparison so the TLC backend (specodelic-ug3) reuses it.
RELATES: specodelic-ug3 (backends) — this must land before any backend's clean verdict is trustworthy; also blocks honest no_counterexample semantics.
Evidence: review round 2, issue 1.

title: CI + publish workflows: gh-actions (just ci gate + cargo publish on v* tags)
description: Genesis-pattern workflows added 2026-09-28: ci.yml (push/PR main, just ci + lint-specs) and publish.yml (tag v* → just ci gate → tag/version match check → cargo package dry-run → cargo publish --locked with CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN). Requires CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN secret in repo settings. Follow-up (separate ticket when taps join): cross-platform binary release + homebrew-charly/scoop-charly tap updates per pretender/espectacular release.yml pattern.

(1) spk feedback — genesis::feedback::handle_feedback, kind arg + --dry-run + --from-last-error, repo charly-vibes/specodelic (espectacular pattern). (2) spk init — write/refresh a <!-- SPECODELIC:START/END --> managed block in the repo's AGENTS.md via genesis::managed_block (espectacular init.rs pattern): lint rule catalog from lint::RULE_TABLE + format_revision + core commands; doctor gains managed-block currency check (block format_revision vs embedded); spk init -f/--force to overwrite user edits. P1: gates the crates.io release.

title: Implement specodelic compile: Set^K -> TOML / TLA+ / proptest functor
description:
Per specs/compile.md. Translate a linted-and-covered spec file's Constraints table into a TOML document, its Model section into a TLA+ (or Alloy) module, and its Properties table into proptest! blocks — without dropping or altering any id.

MUST: ids in == ids out for every compiled file (compile_preserves_ids, no_semantic_drift); a Properties row yields a proptest! block that compiles.
METER: `spk compile <file> --json` exits 0 per file; corpus-wide demo requires specodelic-qc8 closed (precondition_satisfied demands linted+covered).
TASK LADDER (keep ticket whole per compile.md's single Compile transition): 1) Constraints→TOML, 2) Model→TLA+, 3) Properties→proptest!.
TOOLCHAIN: toml crate (already a dep); TLA+ emitted as text (checking it is nx7's job); proptest dep to add.
ANTI-GOALS: never parse prose (prose_untouched); never mint, drop, or alter ids; no orchestration logic here (that's 8kk).
REGRESSION: cargo test — tests/cli.rs + tests/spec_parse.rs keep passing (22 tests).
FILES: src/compile.rs + lib.rs wiring + main.rs Compile subcommand. New/changed files carry Purpose/Responsibilities/Rationale headers. main.rs is shared with nx7/1pv/8kk — one enum arm each; re-anchor base_commit if a sibling pipeline ticket landed first.

Depends on specodelic-qc8: the corpus must reach covered for the end-to-end demo path (compile's own precondition_satisfied).
notes: DEFERRAL (user decision): TLA+ vs Alloy backend deferred to specodelic-mp1 row 6. lnq proceeds with phases 1 (Constraints→TOML) and 3 (Properties→proptest!) + pipeline contract/CLI; model emission (phase 2) is built behind a backend-neutral seam and lands after the mp1 decision. Ticket remains open until the model artifact ships.

title: Reconcile spec corpus with its own Reference Typing table: 48 prose guards, 36 traces_to→Constraint refs, 3 incomplete laws, ~10 row-id token violations
description:
Independent strict reading of the corpus against specs/specodelic.md's Reference Typing table + law_requires_cases (reproduced 2026-09-28, counts within parser noise):

- 48 of 99 transition rows carry a prose guard; the typing table requires guard → Constraint (kind == invariant only).
- 36 constraints.traces_to refs point at Constraint rows; the table says traces_to resolves to Intent only.
- 3 of 7 law properties (coverage_naturality, mapping_naturality, topo_sort_naturality) lack the identity/associativity cases law_requires_cases requires.
- ~10 row ids contain all/every/or tokens against one_capability_per_row / EARS token rules.

Blocked by mp1 because fixing requires deciding (not just editing): does a guard cite a typed constraint or free text? Must reachability land on the file's own intent or any intent (spec itself flags Needs Human Review)? Does kinds.md's 'exactly four fields' for constraints yield to the typing table's supersedes/emits/satisfies, or vice versa? Land each decision as a spec Revision (append-only, per append_only_variants), then fix the corpus rows in the same change, then flip the dogfood gate from advisory to meaningful.
COORDINATES with specodelic-b15: the corpus must pass the COMPLETE linter, so land lint rules (b15) and corpus fixes atomically or lint will red-flag the corpus mid-flight.
Evidence: review round 2, issue 2.

title: Package independent conformance suite into tests/: reference oracle, 50-case lint matrix, structure-aware fuzzer, differential harness
description:
From the 2026-09-28 adversarial review: an independent reference checker built from the spec text, a 50-case conformance matrix (lint correctly flagged 16/42 targeted violations, 3 accidental detections), a structure-aware fuzzer (6,800 command runs, 0 panics/hangs/malformed JSON), and a differential reachability harness (60/60 vs BFS, 25/25 vs real TLC) exist outside the repo. Package them under tests/ so they double as the acceptance gate for:

- specodelic-b15 (lint totality — the matrix is its scoreboard),
- specodelic-8nt / model-check tickets (differential + mutation tests),
- corpus reconciliation (corpus must pass under the strict oracle).

Shapes: matrix cases as data-driven fixtures (case id, corpus fixture, expected rule fired); fuzzer as a #[ignore]d cargo test + a CI nightly job option; TLC differential #[ignore]d locally, opt-in when a JVM exists (coordinate with ug3's TLC backend). Keep each red→green→refactor: land the matrix failing where lint is incomplete is NOT acceptable in CI until b15 closes — gate with #[ignore] + a documented flip.
Evidence: review round 2 closing offer.

title: graph: extract from/to state edges, stop recording typing-forbidden traces_to edges, add blast-radius + staleness, fix init block over-advertising
description:
Reproduced 2026-09-28: spk graph emits only constraints.traces_to / transitions.guard / properties.derives_from edges (405 on the corpus):

1. Never extracts Model/Transitions from→to state edges — the machine shape is invisible to consumers. Add a state-edge kind per specs/graph.md's total_extraction (which names from/to as reference fields).
2. Records 36 constraints.traces_to edges pointing at Constraint rows — the Reference Typing table (specs/specodelic.md) says traces_to resolves to Intent only. Either refuse+report them as labeled violations or route them through ref_kind_compatible once b15 lands; do not silently record forbidden edges.
3. No blast-radius query and no staleness detection — yet the AGENTS.md block that spk init writes advertises 'typed reference graph + blast-radius' (src/blocks.rs:59). Fix the block text to match reality NOW (one-line), implement blast-radius (fan-in/fan-out per node) and graph staleness per specs/graph.md as follow-on.
4. supersedes is declared in the Reference Typing table and graph.md's total_extraction but extracted nowhere (src/ grep: only guide.rs primer) — implement or mark known-gap in the block text.

RED: fixture file with from/to columns → graph emits state edges; fixture with traces_to→constraint → labeled violation, not a silent edge. GREEN: implement; REFACTOR: share ref-extraction with lint (b15's ref_kind_compatible needs the same tables).
TDD note: define the edge-schema test shapes before touching graph.rs.
Evidence: review round 2, issue 3.

title: Tighten output contract: error envelopes carry ok:true, exit-code ambiguity, --human is Rust Debug output, '→ Run: run:' hint duplication
description:
All four reproduced 2026-09-28:

1. ok:true on errors — root cause is upstream genesis-vibes 0.8.1: Output::to_envelope (guide.rs:486) unconditionally calls Envelope::success() even when is_error=true, so JSON reads {"ok":true,"envelope_kind":"error"}. Envelope::error() exists but is never used. Fix in genesis (to_envelope must honor is_error), then specodelic picks it up on the next genesis bump. Genesis repo ticket if there is one; keep a local regression test asserting error envelopes serialize ok:false.
2. Exit code 1 covers both 'lint findings' and 'path not found' — consumers cannot distinguish 'your spec is bad' from 'you typoed the path'. Give not-found/no-files a distinct code (or an explicit machine-readable cause) and document the mapping.
3. --human output is literally Rust {:?} Debug of serde_json::Value (Object { … String(…) }) — render lint/graph/model-check reports as real human text (per-report formatters), keep Debug only for internal logs.
4. Hint rendering duplicates: hints authored as 'run: specodelic graph' emit '→ Run: run: specodelic graph' (genesis Suggestion::fix footer + message()). Either strip a leading 'run: ' at render time or fix authoring convention; also the hint command+description fields duplicate the same text.

RED→GREEN per item; REGRESSION: cargo test suites + snapshot tests for --human output.
Evidence: review round 2, issues 4-5.

description:
Approved OpenSpec change add-embedded-aix-guide (openspec/changes/add-embedded-aix-guide) — tasks.md phase 5; capability delta in specs/doctor/spec.md.

MUST: doctor classifies workspace as self_hosting (specs/specodelic.md exists) vs consumer (otherwise, incl. no specs/); self_hosting keeps today's checks; consumer mode reports embedded format_revision as ok, never fails on the missing core spec, and — when a local corpus exists — extracts its latest Revision N heading (numerically largest trailing integer) and warns (never fails) if newer than FORMAT_REVISION. Corpus with no Revision headings: skip the currency check with an informational note. Empty workspace: consumer mode with an informational spk new hint, exit 0.

Implement model-check backends per model_check.md backend contract: stateright (default, embedded, BFS) and TLC (opt-in JVM); report names engine+version per backend_identified
description: Per model_check.md Notes: implement the TLC opt-in backend (JVM subprocess over the emitted .tla module, -depth as the stated bound) behind the same run-report contract shipped by specodelic-nx7 (RunReport/backend/bound/outcome/.check.json). MUST: a missing checker binary is an ERROR, never a no_counterexample result. Also: cross-backend report comparability (backend_identified) and, once the predicate-fragment decision lands (specodelic-mp1 row), the counterexample path (counterexample_is_minimal via TLC's shortest trace / counterexample_names_violated_invariant).

No backend verdict is trustworthy until 8nt lands. (b) The default backend reports no_counterexample with invariants_checked:[] — see the zero-invariants ticket for the required verdict semantics. (c) TLC opt-in path: review found the emitted .tla header and stuttering behavior need fixes before TLC runs clean; a CI differential test between backends is requested. (d) Differential evidence so far (external harness): 25/25 agreement with real TLC on corpus models; not reproducible in-repo until the conformance suite lands.

title: Decide open spec questions before pipeline v1 (HITL)
description:
HITL ticket — human decisions required before pipeline v1 can be called done. One decision per row; each blocks CLOSING a specific ticket, not starting it.

1. rename.md Needs Human Review: is a batch (whole-namespace) rename one atomic transaction or n independent ones? → gates specodelic-ams close.
2. merge.md Needs Human Review: what does "a human has explicitly approved a flagged merge" mean operationally (review comment, CI gate, role)? → gates specodelic-7oq close.
3. refactor.md Needs Human Review: should "unrelated fan-in" key off the id namespace or physical directory placement? → gates specodelic-3l7 close.
4. orchestrate.md Needs Human Review: does the orchestrator own each file's draft→parsed transition, or stay scoped to parsed→verified? → gates specodelic-8kk close.
5. EXCL-001 (kinds.md): add a kind = "audit" property type via a Revision to specs/kinds.md (not by editing linter-schema_shape.md directly).
6. compile.md: model-checker backend for model_to_tla — TLA+ or Alloy? compile.md says "TLA+ (or Alloy)" without pinning one. Decision lands as a compile.md Revision. → gates the model-emission phase of specodelic-lnq (phases TOML/proptest proceed; ticket stays open) and nx7's checker target.

DELIVERABLE: each decision recorded where the spec says it belongs (Revision + Notes), tickets unblocked by editing their descriptions.
AFK work (lnq TOML+proptest phases, 1pv, b15, qc8) does NOT wait on this ticket.
notes:
ADDED 2026-09-28 (adversarial review round 2) — three more decisions needed before corpus reconciliation (specodelic blocked-by this ticket):
7. Guard typing: does a transition guard cite a typed constraint ([[id]] → kind==invariant) or may it be free prose? Corpus currently has 48/99 prose guards; the Reference Typing table says invariant-only. Decision gates corpus reconciliation.
8. Reachability target: must every row trace to its OWN file's intent, or any intent? specodelic.md flags this 'Needs Human Review' already; the strict reading found ~150/375 rows unreachable from their own file's intent.
9. kinds.md constraint_row_shape says 'exactly {id, kind, expr, traces_to}' (four fields) while the Reference Typing table declares supersedes/emits/satisfies as legal fields — which governs? Also: is supersedes a graph-extractable field (graph.md total_extraction lists it; graph.rs implements nothing for it)?

comments.author: charly vibes
comments.text: Row 7 (new, from add-model-check Decision 3 A): executable predicate fragment. Native stateright backend ships with invariants_checked: [] — prose guards/predicates are uninterpreted. The counterexample leg (synthetic violated invariant => trace naming the Constraints-table id) needs an executable guard/predicate fragment: options were A (defer — approved for nx7 v0, 2026-09-28), B ([[ref]]-only guard fragment — dead machinery), C (user-supplied Rust predicates; format change, Revision bump — candidate when counterexamples become real). see openspec/changes/add-model-check/design.md

title: Complete specodelic lint: model_shape, graph_shape, reference typing, external_completeness
description:
Per specs/linter-model_shape.md, specs/linter-graph_shape.md, the Reference Typing table in specs/specodelic.md, and specs/linter-external_completeness.md — four specced checkers with no implementation, all required before orchestrate (8kk) can gate correctly.

MUST: every constraint in those four checker files has a corresponding lint rule: model_shape (every_state_used, every_transition_valid, model_sections_paired), graph_shape (acyclic, no_self_ref, single_root_reachable, supersedes_dag), reference typing (ref_kind_compatible — advisory/effect constraints can never gate; emits→effect only; supersedes same-kind), external_completeness (checklist_well_formed, covered_maps_resolve, every_item_accounted, no_duplicate_claim, waiver_has_rationale — optional, non-gating).
METER: `spk lint specs --json` reports zero findings for those rules on the corpus (new known-issues list replaces today's); synthetic fixtures prove each rule fires.
ANTI-GOALS: never parse prose; never add rules the checker specs don't state; external_completeness never gates a stage.
REGRESSION: cargo test — existing suites keep passing.
FILES: src/lint.rs (and src/graph.rs if reachability helpers are shared). File-header required.
notes: EMPIRICAL BASELINE 2026-09-28 (adversarial review round 2): against a 42-case targeted-violation matrix built from this repo's own checker specs, current lint fires correctly on only 16; 3 more 'detections' were accidental (unrelated rule). The corpus itself passes with ZERO findings while containing (strict reading): 48/99 prose guards, 36 traces_to→Constraint refs, 3/7 laws missing identity/associativity, ~10 row-id token violations. The METER above ('zero findings on corpus') is therefore insufficient alone — add the 50-case matrix (see conformance-suite ticket) as the scoreboard. Also per review: reject unknown kinds/columns/cell counts, validate id charsets, make file discovery loud (report skipped files, tolerate BOMs), and enforce no_boolean_columns/non-recursive lint invocation (specodelic-6pi) before any CI gate chains lint.

title: Implement specodelic merge: id collisions + dangling renames pre-merge
description:
Per specs/merge.md. Detect what a textual git merge can't see: id collisions between branches and renames left dangling by references minted elsewhere, before reporting a merge complete.

MUST: a two-branch fixture with an id collision is flagged; a rename left dangling by a reference minted on the other branch is flagged; a clean merge reports no findings.
METER: integration test with two tempdir spec trees + `spk merge --json` findings; cargo test.
ANTI-GOALS: don't re-derive the reference graph (graph_reused_not_rederived — consume graph.rs); don't gate on findings the spec doesn't gate on.
HITL: what "a human has explicitly approved a flagged merge" means operationally — see specodelic-mp1 before closing.
FILES: src/merge.rs; reuse graph.rs. File-header required.

title: Implement specodelic orchestrate: lint->compile->model_check->verify driver
description:
Per specs/orchestrate.md. Drive the six Checker Ownership checkers in dependency order (skip dependents on failure, run independent branches regardless), then coverage, compile, model_check, verify in sequence — gating each stage transition on the exact guards specs/specodelic.md specifies, never looser or stricter. external_completeness runs when a checklist exists but never gates. rename stays out of scope.

MUST: a corpus run reports each stage's outcome; the first failing stage halts its dependents (skipped, not failed) while independent branches still report; stage sequence matches specodelic.md's lifecycle (draft → parsed → linted → compiled → model_checked → verified).
METER: `spk orchestrate specs --json` → .data lists every stage with status; halt/skip behavior proven by a synthetic fixture with one failing checker.
ANTI-GOALS: no looser/stricter gating than specified; no rename triggering; no silent skips (every skip is reported).
REGRESSION: cargo test — existing suites keep passing.
FILES: src/orchestrate.rs + main.rs Orchestrate subcommand (file-header required; shared main.rs with sibling pipeline tickets).

Depends on specodelic-1pv (last pipeline stage) and specodelic-b15 (all six Checker Ownership checkers must exist first). HITL: whether the orchestrator also owns draft→parsed — see specodelic-mp1 before closing.

title: Implement specodelic rename: atomic id rename with link rewrite
description:
Per specs/rename.md. Single (old_id, new_id) request: update the defining row and every referencing [[link]] atomically, or leave the repo unchanged. Ends in a verify step re-running linter.referential_integrity and linter.graph_shape (i.e. `spk graph` + `spk lint` — the linters, NOT the pipeline verify command).

MUST: after a successful rename, `spk graph specs --json` .data.dangling length == 0 and the new id resolves everywhere the old one did; on a failed precondition every file is byte-identical to before (all-or-nothing).
METER: rename integration test on a tempdir fixture (definition + cross-file links) + the graph check above.

title: Implement specodelic verify: execute proptest blocks + gate
description:
Per specs/verify.md. Run every proptest! block compile produced to completion; transition a file to verified only when all pass AND model_check's most recent run against the CURRENT compiled artifact is clean.

MUST: a file with a failing proptest block is NOT verified; a file whose model_check result is stale (artifact changed since the run) is NOT verified; only the conjunction verifies.
METER: `spk verify <file> --json` → .data.status == "verified" exactly in that case, else the blocking stage is named.
ANTI-GOALS: never bypass the model_check guard; never cache/assume artifacts are current; never treat a skipped stage as passed.
REGRESSION: cargo test — existing suites keep passing.

title: Implement specodelic model-check: TLC/Alloy against compiled module
description:
Per specs/model_check.md. Run the model checker against compile's output; report no_counterexample-within-bound or counterexample (TLC path). Distinguish model_checked (a run happened) from no_counterexample (no violation) — CLAR-003.

IMPLEMENTED (add-model-check, Decision 3 Option A approved): spk model-check <files> [--max-depth 100] [--max-states] [--timeout-secs] — native stateright backend interprets the compiled ModelIR as a pc-automaton (init = first listed state, transitions as always-enabled actions, matching the committed .tla semantics); explores exhaustively within the bound; reached cap => timed_out (never collapsed into clean); missing compiled artifact => labeled missing_artifact error with a spk compile hint; run reports persist as <stem>.check.json carrying the consumed .tla's SHA-256 for verify's staleness check (rerun_on_model_change).

AMENDED MUST per approval: the corpus language has no executable predicate semantics, so the native backend checks no user invariants and reports invariants_checked: [] honestly; the counterexample leg (synthetic spec with violated invariant yields trace naming the invariant) is DEFERRED to the predicate-fragment decision — new HITL row on specodelic-mp1; TLC backend moved to specodelic-ug3.

description:
